speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat
text: asked the Minister for National Development (a) what is the rationale for requiring 75% support level from eligible households for the Neighbourhood Renewal Programme (NRP) where residents do not need to co-pay; and (b) whether the Ministry will consider setting a timeline for the calling of a tender for NRP works when the NRP for the precinct is announced.

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
text: Would the Minister consider reviewing the 75% support level?

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
text: Because the awareness of NRP is already achieved through 100% direct mailing to the houses.

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
text: We also have two exhibitions, the Public Consultation  and Consensus Gathering.

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
text: Furthermore, the NRP plan would have undergone multiple reviews even by the Housing and Development Board and then also taken into consideration the wish list from the Town Councils, residents, Members of Parliament, the Residents' Committees.

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
text: So, that plan itself is almost like optimised for that precinct.

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
text: So, would the Ministry consider reviewing that 75% requirement, even 50%?

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
text: Because when we do house visits, a lot of residents asked us why they still need to vote when they do not need to pay for this external thing.

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
text: They also said that they were also not consulted.

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
text: For example, they do not need to vote whether they want the silver zone or—

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Getting the residents aware of the project through direct mailers, exhibitions, community consultation is but one important part of that process.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Getting feedback and ultimately persuading residents that this plan benefits them is best evidenced through residents' support for the proposal.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: If you reduce or do away with the poll requirement, then the question is how certain are we all that these facilities, indeed, are welcomed, or are needed by the residents?

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Even though the residents do not have to pay for these improvements, they relate to that immediate lived environment and I think they ought to have a say.
